reviews.text: So professional, so kind

My dog was taken care of by Dr. Olson and her great assistant for an evening visit. I expected, given my dog’s old age and several chronic conditions, we were in for a battery of tests and a long night. After the doctor’s examination, and treatment with the technician, I was happy to hear that my dog just needed some medications, some grooming and a medicated paw bath. It was such a relief and my dog is much better. I know it could have been a totally different outcome, but half the relief came from the doctor’s patience and explanations, which were very comforting and the technician was very good about making sure I was prepared for the at home care. Thank you Dr Olson and team at Burnham Park Animal Hospital!
Attentive staff and knowledgeable doctors
It is a professional facility.
Clean and well organized check in process.  Friendly staff and knowledgeable and empathetic vet.  Pet plans available to defer costs if needed.

I brought my cat in for routine blood work, and the negligence and lack of care that followed have been unacceptable. Following the blood draw, an exposed area was left with rubbing alcohol residue on her fur/skin. Because cats groom obsessively, she licked and ingested it, which immediately triggered nausea and caused her to stop eating completely. When I reached out regarding her sudden deterioration, the clinic was utterly unhelpful and took zero accountability for the issue their careless handling caused. The vet actually left me a voicemail gaslighting me and telling me I’m lying and that my own cat had another issue that was causing this! Mind you she NEVER had this issue until she came here! I called another vet and they said that it was IN FACT the rubbing alcohol triggering this for my cat! Because of this, l had to find another veterinary care treat a complication that should never have happened. If you value attentive, safe, and accountable care for your pets, take them somewhere else.

SCAM ALERT - This is the most financially predatory vet clinic I have EVER been to. If you want to guarantee your pet actually receives the care you pay for, do not go here. I was seeking affordable pet care for my aging dog. During my first visit, I was repeatedly pressured to sign up for the paw plan. And because of my dog’s age, I agreed because they assured me that the plan was in my dog’s best interest. What they did NOT explain was that they PICK and CHOOSE which services to provide AFTER you sign up and pay.  My dog needs dental care and I have been refused TWICE in spite of paying monthly. When I called to politely request a cancellation of the plan, they informed me that I would still owe the TOTAL paw plan amount of $1600. And the only thing my dog has received is shots and bloodwork (that was done as a precaution but not necessary because she just came in for allergies and dental!).

The issue is that the cost of the extra bloodwork was NOT explained to me, and it totaled over $400. Instead, they rushed me into signing up for the paw plan - so that it would SEEM LIKE I was getting a discount, when the FULL cost of services not explained is hidden in monthly payments extended over a year.

I’m completely heartbroken that I was pressured to sign up for this plan and was not told the honest truth about what it covers - ESPECIALLY for someone with an aging pet. I was also pressured to get blood tests done that she did not need, which came back completely fine. So I’m stuck with a $1600 plan that my dog cannot benefit from. This place is 100% PROFIT over PETS.

I’ve been bringing my cat here since she was a baby and I always leave comfortable knowing she had the best care! We recently worked with Dr Stone who diagnosed her CCL injury and has been available to answer all my questions. I would easily recommend them to others! I’ve also been on their paw plan and it gives me the peace of mind I need that my cat is healthy and has a full evaluation at every annual exam!
We are honored to have provided care for Paco at Burnham Park Animal Hospital. Thank you for your rating.

We sincerely value your 5-star rating. Your support means a great deal to our team at Burnham Park Animal Hospital.
Amazing care and team.  Thanks for taking Warrior on an emergency basis.  Highly recommend!

Love this place and the Veterinarians here are great.
Beautiful facilities. Professional, a friendly team who treat my pets with care. Highly recommended

AVOID AT ALL COST! THEY ARE SCAM ARTISTS! They sell you on their "plan" and when you need to see a vet you find out it covers nothing. Then when you try to cancel the plan, they over charge you for the "services" they provided so you have no choice but to pay the marked up fees for unnecessary services they offered, thinking it was covered. Also, the vets are quite incompetent. They couldn't answer multiple questions regarding our dog that gets seizures and recommended seizure causing medication which other vets said was unacceptable. If your pet needs prescriptions, be very wary of Burnham Park. My experience of their vet care has been excellent (annual exam and teeth cleaning). My experience of getting a prescription has been terrible. They have zero cost transparency, poor communication, and staff who are not knowledgeable about pricing even when asked. My dog has been a patient here since January. Every October she gets allergies and has taken Apoquel in the past, which, at her last vet, they were very clear about the price and how filling it worked (either at their office or Chewy), so I am familiar with the price (approx $3 per tablet). I called Burnham Park last week and explained that she hadn't needed Apoquel till now and I wanted to know how prescriptions worked here. The staff on the phone said she'd write a note to the vet - great. I later get a text saying that the medication has been approved by the doctor, you may stop by anytime to pick it up. I was surprised pick up was the only option, but that's fine! I went in this morning to pick it up and the desk staff said it would be $122.95. I was very surprised so I asked if she could explain how many tablets I'm getting - she said 30. I said "hmm, it used to be about $3 a tablet so that would be $90, so is it $4 a pill now?" She didn't answer and just said "It's an expensive medication". (It would have been ideal of her to mention that there is an office fill fee and tell me the tablet price). I said okay, you can charge my card and asked for a receipt. Later today, I reviewed my receipt hoping it would be ITEMIZED. Nope. It did not indicate the tablet price or that there was any fill fee, just one line item of $122.95. I go on google to check the current price of Apoquel. In doing so, I realize Burnham Park has its own online pharmacy on the website, which I was not informed was an option (when I specifically called to ask about how to get a prescription!) and I notice that it is $2.95 a tablet, or $93 dollars for 30 days. In order to understand the discrepancy between $93 and $122.95, I call Burnham and give my info and then ask if she can explain the cost breakdown for that invoice. She cannot. She simply says online prices are different because of promotions and autoship. I explain that the $93 price is the price before autoship, but that yes I understand there will be some price discrepancy. She then says "oh, well there's also a fill fee at the office" (the FIRST time this has been mentioned. She does not mention the amount.). I then ask "Can you please tell me the tablet price for what I paid in office?". She says she doesn't know. I then ask about the fill fee and she says "The fill fee is a flat $15". Okay FINALLY that is approaching an itemization of the invoice. I'm like okay... but I still need the tablet price. If it were to be $93 for the meds and $15 for the fee, then that's $108. How are we getting from $108 to $122.95? There are no taxes on meds. I then ask why, when I called to ask about how to fill a prescription, I was only given one option and thus had to pay $122.95... THIRTY DOLLARS MORE than Burnham's own online pharmacy which they didn't tell me about. I acknowledge that price discrepancies exist (yes, the Burnham tablet price might be higher) and I understand that I also did not do my due diligence in asking if there were other options. However, the issue remains that the office staff is UNABLE to give me an ITEMIZED INVOICE or even verbally tell me a tablet price or disclose the fill fee up front - only when prodded repeatedly on the phone. When you are selling something in a quantity of 30, it is absurd that they do not have a computer system that is taking a tablet price and multiplying it by 30. Based on the utter lack of information the staff could provide, they could just be randomly deciding on the number $122.95. The vet care might be great, but their bookkeeping, transparency, honesty, and desk staff training seems poor.

We are done with Burnham Park AH hospital and with Dr. Schell. We have been with them for a bit over two years. Recently we brought in our dog due to blood in her urine:

Dr. Schell recommended an ultrasound and diagnosed her with possible cancer and possibly only a few months to live. He sent us home with antibiotics and pain medication. Learning of our dog’s diagnosis was shocking. I missed an entire workday because of it. My sister-in-law even flew in to say goodbye.

After four weeks, we returned for a follow-up visit. Dr. Schell suggested a cadet bref test. The results were negative. He then changed his approach, thinking it could be bladder stones, and recommended an X-ray. I asked if the X-ray could differentiate between bladder stones and cancer, and he confirmed it. So why did we go through all this trouble instead of doing the X-ray right away?

I’m deeply disappointed, feeling betrayed and even scammed. We spent over $1000 on Dr. Schell’s misdiagnosis and inappropriate recommendations.

UPDATE: I can no longer give Burnham 5 stars. I have been coming to Burnham since 2020. At some point they dropped the ball on giving my cats leukemia shots and now I have to bring them back in for boosters, which of course is additional time and an additional charge. I am very unhappy about this. I cannot trust them to maintain the correct vaccine regimen for my pets.

I have been to Burnham many times. I recommend Burnham based on the excellent service that I have received, the quality of their veterinarians/veterinary staff, the long hours the hospital keeps, the cleanliness of the facility, and the ease of making an appointment. I have not had a bad experience yet. The two vets I see are Dr. Phillips and Dr. Vlahos. They always take their time to address all my questions, are great about following up, provide thorough examinations and recommendations, etc. The hospital is nice and clean. It has actually been newly remodeled. Sometimes you have to wait a bit to see a doctor after you come in but when I had an urgent matter they were able to see me that day so I don't mind being patient if they have to squeeze an appointment in around me due to an emergency. The staff are doing the best they can to accommodate everyone; some grace goes a long way during these trying times. If you want to be seen right away it is probably best to schedule an appointment time that is first thing in the morning. It is very easy to make an appointment on their website and you can schedule an appointment up to about a month out. I have never seen a non-emergency vet clinic that keeps the hours they do; 8am-8pm Mon-Thurs and various hours on the weekend as well! Also, the vets themselves perform teeth cleanings which is something I have also not experienced in the past (my former vet office used a pet dental technician). Of course I would rather have a licensed veterinarian cleaning my pet's teeth! I believe this hospital offers very good value given its location in the city. You get what you pay for.
